title: Mechanical Systems: Levers and Linkages
summary: Effort, load and fulcrum, the three classes of levers, mechanical advantage, the law of the lever, and linkages that change the direction of movement.

notes.text: A **mechanism** is a device that changes one kind of movement or force into another, making work easier. A **lever** is a rigid bar that turns about a fixed point called the **fulcrum** (pivot).

items: **Load**: the object or resistance being moved.

rows: See-saw, crowbar, scissors, pliers, claw hammer pulling a nail
Tweezers, fishing rod, braai tongs, your forearm

notes.label: Memory aid
notes.text: **F-L-E** for 1, 2, 3: in a 1st-class lever the **F**ulcrum is in the middle, in a 2nd-class lever the **L**oad is in the middle, in a 3rd-class lever the **E**ffort is in the middle.

notes.caption: A first-class lever: a long effort arm lifts a heavy load with a small effort

notes.title: Classifying levers
notes.problem: Classify a seesaw, a wheelbarrow and tweezers. Ask what is in the middle.
steps: Seesaw: the fulcrum is in the middle, so class 1.
Wheelbarrow: the load is in the middle, so class 2.
Tweezers: the effort is in the middle, so class 3.
notes.answer: Seesaw class 1, wheelbarrow class 2, tweezers class 3.

notes.text: If **MA > 1**, the lever multiplies force: a small effort moves a large load (crowbar, wheelbarrow). If **MA < 1**, more effort is needed but the load moves further and faster (tweezers, fishing rod: third-class levers).

notes.caption: The arms are the distances from the fulcrum

notes.title: Calculating effort
notes.problem: A crowbar is used to lift a 600 N rock. The rock is 0,2 m from the fulcrum and the effort is applied 1,2 m from the fulcrum. Calculate the effort needed and the mechanical advantage.

notes.text: A **linkage** is a set of levers (links) joined together with pivots to transfer and change movement.

rows: Makes the output move in the opposite direction to the input
Output moves in the same direction as the input and stays parallel
Toolbox trays, ironing boards, car windscreen wipers
Changes the direction of movement through 90°
Changes back-and-forth (reciprocating) motion into rotary motion
